meta.title: Cessna 172P fuselage structure as 3D geometry (reference airplane 1983, s/n 17275500)
sources: Cessna D2065-3-13 (Cessna Model 172 Series 1977-1986 Service Manual, Rev 3): Fig 1-2 (pdf 14) stations; Section 18 paras 18-55..18-63 (pdf 498-500), Figs 18-4, 18-5, 18-12 (pdf 513-532); Fig 5-1 (pdf 176); Figs 4-1, 4-2 and paras 4-14..4-19 (pdf 162-172); Fig 11-2 (pdf 281); Figs 3-1, 3-5, 3-6, 3-9 (pdf 125-158); Fig 2-2 / para 2-3, 2-7 (pdf 38-40). Facts and page references only.
FlightGear c172p (GPL-2.0): assets/c172p.glb, assets/cockpit.glb - outer-skin shape (local only)
data/c172-stations.json (station -> model transform, scale 1 along FS)
data/c172p-airframe-placements.json (attach bolts the structure carries); data/c172p-harness.json, c172p-fuel-3d.json, c172p-controls-3d.json, c172p-instruments-3d.json (items cleared / cut out for)
meta.frame: raw AC3D frame of Models/c172-common.ac: meters, +x aft, +y up, +z toward the LEFT wing (same as assets/c172p.glb)

geometry_types.plate: 2D outline (+holes) in the plane origin + x*axes[0] + y*axes[1], extruded `thickness` along axes[0] x axes[1] (machine.js 'plate')
geometry_types.tank: triangle mesh {vertices, faces} for built-up members (channels, angles, stringers, fittings): one mesh per member, rendered by machine.js like the fuel tanks

meta.method: Stations true (Fig 1-2), planes normal to the FS axis; section outlines from FlightGear's skin less 0.032 in; webs punched where routed items pass (item radius + 3.5 mm), plus lightening holes; swept members built from short planar plates; see the module docstring.

sourced: bulkhead stations FS 0.00, 8.12, 16.66, 44.00, 56.70, 65.33, 80.00, 90.00, 108.00, 124.00, 142.00, 178.00, 205.81, 228.68 (Fig 1-2); which run full height vs below the floor (dashed-line lengths)
semimonocoque: formed bulkheads, stringers, reinforcing channels, skins (18-55); seat rails are structure (18-58)
gear bulkheads FS 56.70 / 65.33 with inboard and outboard forgings between them, deep webs with lightening holes, irregular cut-outs for cables and fuel lines (Fig 5-1, 18-60)
firewall material MIL-S-5059 18-8 CRES, periphery angles lapping the skin, upper and lower diagonal support angles, engine-mount attach at 4 points (18-62, Fig 18-12, Fig 11-2)
stringer (bulb / Z) and channel (flanged lightening hole) section shapes (Fig 18-5); skin gauges .020-.051 (Fig 18-4)
fin front spar bolts to the FS 205.81 bulkhead; fin rear spar and stabilizer rear spar to tailcone fittings; forward stabilizer bolts (4-14..4-19)
wing attach: front spar AN8-23, rear spar AN7-24 with eccentric bushings (Fig 4-1); strut fuselage attachment fitting (Fig 4-2)
estimated: every member's section size and gauge except the firewall material (no dimensions printed)
forward door post line (no FS printed: follows FlightGear's door edge), roof bows, carry-through stations (next to the placed attach bolts), longeron / stringer count and layout
frame outlines (FlightGear skin; the manual has no section dimensions)
FS 116 closeout frame (FlightGear panel, not a manual station)

skin_deviations.note: The manual prints no fuselage cross-section dimensions (no WL/BL diagram, para 1-5 / c172-stations.json), so FlightGear's cross-sections cannot be checked directly; deviations > 1.5 cm are listed where the manual gives a station or dimension. Frame outlines follow FlightGear's skin; stations, member sections and gauges are kept true; members stand proud of FlightGear's skin only where noted per component (external fittings).

rows.flightgear: FlightGear firewall plate at transform FS 3.6-6.6 (upper / lower panel)
rows.note: an ERROR of the fitted station->model transform near the nose (its fit points R1-R4 constrain FS only at 3.4, 90, 108, 229 in; the firewall, which defines FS 0.00, is not one of them): the airplane's FS 0.00 is FlightGear's firewall plate, where the engine mount, battery box, contactors, strainer and grommets are mounted
rows.structure: structural firewall built ON FlightGear's plate (its bends kept); forward frames shifted by the same correction tapering linearly from 3.65 in at FS 0 to 0 at FS 20 (FS 8.12 -> model 10.29, FS 16.66 -> model 17.27); longerons and stringers start at the plate

rows.feature: Aft door post / aft gear bulkhead
rows.structure: frame at FS 65.33: the FlightGear door overlaps it by ~0.85 in (as a door laps its post)

rows.feature: Rear window aft tip / aft cabin bulkhead
rows.structure: bulkhead at FS 108.00 crosses FlightGear's rear glass 4.5 in forward of its tip

rows.feature: Fuselage half-width at the wing root (cabin top)
rows.manual: wing root rib WS 23.62 (Fig 1-2) - if the rib abuts the fuselage side
rows.note: the manual does not state that the root rib is at the skin; FlightGear's wing_center fills the gap
rows.structure: frame outlines follow FlightGear's skin (the manual prints no section dimensions); a wider true cabin is possible but not documented

rows.note: FlightGear lateral scale at the gear ~0.875 (c172-stations.json)
rows.structure: forgings placed on the model's strut bolts
stations are scale 1 along FS; no effect

rows.note: the controls agent put its bulkhead fairleads on this panel (FS 116.1)
rows.structure: light frame added at FS 116.0, flagged as not a manual station

flightgear_gear_struts.note: holes are cut where FlightGear's struts pass through the gear structure (forgings are bored by them)

inside_skin.method: each vertex's radial distance from the station-section centre vs FlightGear's skin radius at that polar angle (0.5 in station steps)
